name: Velvaris
manufacturer: Street chemist collective — the Gray Zone district 7 (branded 'Ironwake Labs')
description: Velvaris is a the Gray Zone-born compound developed by the Ironwake Labs collective — a loose network of unlicensed chemists operating in GLMZ's District 7 industrial zone. It dramatically amplifies tactile sensation, making touch feel profound and consuming — fabric feels like water, human contact feels overwhelming in the best possible way, and the chronic pain from labor injuries or ill-fitted chrome temporarily dissolves into warmth. It is the drug of people who work with their bodies and whose bodies hurt.
effects: chronic pain relief through sensation recontextualization (pain signals remain but are interpreted as warmth)
profound pleasure from human physical contact
sense of bodily comfort and safety
reduced psychological distress related to body image or augmentation dysphoria
side_effects: dangerous thermal desensitization — users cannot accurately gauge heat or pain during effect, leading to burns and injuries
chrome interface interference — dermal sensors in augmented limbs can feedback-amplify and cause localized pain spikes
the collective has no quality control and batch potency varies significantly
cultural_context: Velvaris is tenderness as contraband. On the Gray Zone, where physical labor destroys bodies, where chrome is fitted cheap and chafes, where human touch is sometimes the only luxury available — Velvaris is used communally, between people who trust each other. Ironwake Labs has become something close to a folk institution in District 7; they distribute sliding-scale prices and have a reputation for pulling bad batches voluntarily. Tier 1 medics have a complicated relationship with Velvaris — it causes injuries but it also keeps people going.
story_hooks: Lazarus's acquisition team has identified Ironwake Labs as a target — not to shut them down but to buy their formulation and reformulate it for Tier 3-4 at a hundred times the price; the collective has refused, and now one of their chemists has been approached privately

A thermal desensitization injury from a bad Velvaris batch has killed a the Gray Zone worker — her family is trying to pursue something like justice, but Ironwake is also their community, and the complexity is real

A Tier 3 journalist embedded in District 7 to write a piece on Ironwake Labs has started using Velvaris themselves — and is now three weeks past deadline, not answering messages, and reportedly doing just fine
